line: Crowley on Malkuth (The Book of Thoth); Jung on Malchuth in CW14; von Franz on the sephiroth in Number and Time.

sections.title: Crowley's Tens
sections.line: Crowley on the Tens and Malkuth, and Assiah: The Book of Thoth, pdf p181 and p195.

quotes.quote: These cards are attributed to Malkuth.
The number Ten refers to Malkuth, which depends from the other nine Sephiroth,
So far as the Sephira is concerned, it is right down in the world of Assiah.

sections.title: Earth and the planetary attribution
sections.line: Crowley on Malkuth, Earth, the planetary attribution and the number Ten in the diagram: The Book of Thoth, pdf p181, p266 and p23.

quotes.quote: There is now no planetary attribution to consider.
The tenth Sephira, which refers to Earth, is not shown on this figure.
It is the number Ten suspended from the 7, 8, 9 in the diagram.

sections.title: Malkuth on the throne of Binah
sections.line: Crowley on Malkuth and the throne of Binah: The Book of Thoth, pdf p123.

quotes.quote: Malkuth shall be uplifted and set upon the throne of Binah.

sections.title: Jung's Malchuth
sections.line: Jung on Malchuth as the underlying feminine principle, and Knorr von Rosenroth on the name: CW14 ¶18 and ¶640.

quotes.quote: Malchuth, conforming to the archetypal pattern, is the underlying feminine principle
the name of the last Sefira, and Malchuth herself, the Kingdom, are so called

sections.title: Von Franz on the ten
sections.line: Von Franz on the ten primal numbers, the sephiroth: von Franz, Number and Time, pdf p95.

quotes.quote: the ten primal numbers, the sephiroth, are considered to be emanations of divine immaterial origin
They are “spheres” and “totalities” of the unknowable primal one
